newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Four dead, one missing in Wellington boat tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Four dead, one missing in Wellington boat tragedy.

text.p: Four people were killed and one was missing after a fishing boat and a container ship collided near the entrance to Wellington harbour, officials said on Monday.
Police said the four were believed to have been trapped in the upturned hull of the boat. Their bodies had been recovered by divers.
One person from the fishing boat, as yet unnamed, had been winched to safety soon after the collision, but police divers were still searching for others early this morning.
Inspector Pat O'Neill of Wellington police said the collision happened at 10.40 p.m. on Sunday.
"As a result, the fishing vessel overturned. One person has been recovered alive," he said.
The container ship, the Australian-owned Sydney Express, was entering Wellington Harbour when the collision occurred.
The entrance channel where the collision took place is about 1.5 km wide.
The Westpac rescue helicopter and an interisland ferry were involved in the search operation. Tugs and the ferry trained spotlights on the water as divers and rescuers in smaller boats searched.
The collision occurred as the leading boat in the BT Global Challenge yacht race prepared to enter Wellington harbour later on Monday.
